name: L1e-A Powered Cycle
description: A pedal cycle past the EAPC limits whose motor, of no more than 1,000 W, mainly aids pedalling and cuts out by 25 km/h: an L1e-A powered cycle under the UK's assimilated copy of Regulation (EU) No 168/2013. It's a motor vehicle, so it must be approved, registered, taxed and insured, and its rider needs a category Q licence and, on two wheels, a motorcycle helmet.

restrictions.rule: A cycle designed to be pedalled, with an auxiliary motor whose main aim is to aid pedalling; three- and four-wheeled ones meeting the same limits count as L1e-A too
The motor's output cuts off at or below 25 km/h
A maximum continuous rated or net power of no more than 1,000 W
Past the EAPC limits, as with a motor over 250 W; one within them, including a type-approved twist-and-go, is an electrically assisted pedal cycle instead
restrictions.citation: Electrically Assisted Pedal Cycles Regulations 1983, SI 1983/1168, reg. 4, as amended by SI 2015/24, reg. 2

restrictions.rule: A motor vehicle, so one first used from January 2016 must be type approved, or get a Motorcycle Single Vehicle Approval, before it can be registered; an approved one shows its approval number
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 189(1)(c); Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 (assimilated), art. 2(1)

restrictions.rule: Must be registered with the DVLA and taxed, at the zero-emission motorcycle rate
Must be insured for use on a road or other public place; an uninsured one may be seized

The rider needs a licence covering category Q (fewer than four wheels, a maximum design speed of no more than 25 km/h), from age 16; a full AM, A or car (B) licence includes it, and a provisional licence holder can't carry a passenger
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 87; Motor Vehicles (Driving Licences) Regulations 1999, SI 1999/2864, regs. 3(1), 9(1A), 16(6), Sch. 2

restrictions.rule: On a two-wheeled one, the rider and any passenger must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting BS 6658:1985 or UNECE Regulation 22.05 or 22.06, unless a Sikh wearing a turban
restrictions.citation: Motor Cycles (Protective Helmets) Regulations 1998, SI 1998/1807, reg. 4; Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 16(2)

restrictions.rule: Needs an MOT test certificate once it's three years past first registration
Ridden only on the road: not on cycle tracks, cycle lanes or pavements
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 21; Roads (Scotland) Act 1984, s. 129(5)

restrictions.rule: In Northern Ireland too it's a motorcycle or moped: it must be type approved, registered, taxed and insured, and its rider needs a driving licence and a motorcycle helmet
